READABILITY.evidence: Names are clear (buildWindowClause, validateWindowName, WindowDefinition). Public methods have JSDoc with examples, e.g. 'Adds a named window definition to the `window` clause'. Formatting matches the codebase (dprint was run). Single-letter names (q, m, s) appear only in tests.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: Good structure: one shared buildWindowClause and validateWindowName, and each dialect only adds a field, a thin method and one chunk. But the committed test keeps debug and dead code: `console.log(q.sql);` and an unused `const dialect = new PgDialect(); ... void dialect;`.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: Inputs are validated at every boundary: ntile/nthValue arguments, window names (empty and whitespace-only), frame from/to order, and invalid unboundedFollowing/unboundedPreceding positions. preceding/following and lag/lead offsets are also checked. Numbers are inlined rather than bound; the test asserts `expect(q.params).toEqual([])`.

C6-02-CASE1.evidence: Purely additive. Helpers are exported via sql/functions/index.ts. An optional `windows?: WindowDefinition[]` is added to all five *SelectConfig types, and the same `window(name, spec = {}): this` is on pg, mysql, sqlite, singlestore and gel. windowSql is undefined when no windows are set, so SQL for existing queries is unchanged.
